damn did you install ALL the updates ever?

This occurs because Windows keeps patch/update .msi files around so that you can uninstall updates if you want. They then periodically release rollups that put a bunch of these into one update, but if you already installed the individual updates, it doesnt delete the old msi's. For average PC users, just delete these. Keeping these around is really only worth it for large enterprises where KB7573874 blows up CrappyApp.exe that they run their business on, and they want to uninstall a single KB instead of updating their app they wrote in 1992 in some guy's garage.

This (minus that insanely obscene file size) is actually normal practice. Most Linux distributions/package managers follow similar practices in case an update bricks your system, that way you can roll back to an older package.
